requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: Four changes. First, in TypeCollector, the two member-collection loops now `continue` after reporting the mixed int/string key diagnostic. Second, the same loops skip the dictionary `Add` when a duplicate int or string key is already present, instead of throwing. Third, new analyzer tests check that `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types still get MsgPack004, MsgPack015, MsgPack003 and MsgPack005, and do not get MsgPack011, MsgPack016 or MsgPack017. Fourth, there are new execution tests and a README section that documents the behaviour.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stopped reporting anything for suppressed types after 3.1.1. The code change hardens the collector against two crashes. One is `Dictionary.Add` throwing on a duplicate key. The other is `intKey!.Value` running when the key kinds are mixed. An analyzer exception would silence all diagnostics. None of the visible source hunks mentions SuppressSourceGeneration, so it is not shown how this fix connects to the reported regression.
touches_beyond_requirement: The crash hardening (continue, plus guarded Add) applies to all [MessagePackObject] types, not only suppressed ones.
A README section documents which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types, including MsgPack012, which no test covers.
An execution test checks round-tripping through the dynamic resolver.
story.confidence_overview: High that the guarded Adds and the `continue` prevent the specific exceptions. Medium-to-low that this alone fixes the reported regression: no visible hunk touches a SuppressSourceGeneration skip, so the analyzer tests are the only evidence that diagnostics now fire for suppressed types. The round-trip execution test is weak; it only asserts non-null.

findings.description: Claim C15 disputed: C15 states that the source change is limited to the two member loops in TypeCollector, but its citation (TypeCollector.cs lines 1004-1042) covers only the first member loop (including unchanged lines 1010-1021 and 1027-1037) and completely omits the second member loop changed at lines 1144-1183.

No visible hunk references SuppressSourceGeneration. If the 3.1.1 regression came from an early return or skip for suppressed types elsewhere, this diff does not remove it. The crash hardening would then not explain why MsgPack004, MsgPack015 and MsgPack003 now fire for suppressed types. The owner should confirm that the analyzer tests actually pass and fail without the change.

The `continue` skips every later check for that member, including the formatter attribute lookup and member-type validation such as MsgPack003. Further diagnostics on a mixed-key member are therefore lost.

The duplicate int-key member is dropped silently. This relies on a duplicate-key diagnostic having been reported earlier in a check that is not visible in the diff, so it cannot be verified here that the int path reports one.
The second loop's changes (lines 1145-1182) are not exercised by any new test.
The round-trip test only asserts NotNull. It would pass even if Id or Name were lost, so it does not verify correct serialization.
The README claims MsgPack012 is still reported for suppressed types, but no test covers that.

README.md documents that MsgPack012 (types accessible to the resolver) is still validated when SuppressSourceGeneration = true, but unlike MsgPack004, MsgPack005, MsgPack015, and MsgPack003, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs contains no test verifying MsgPack012 on a suppressed type. Because MsgPack012 checks resolver accessibility and companion partial-type checks (MsgPack011) are skipped when no formatter is generated, this documented behavior is unverified and may not actually hold.

In both member loops (lines 1035 and 1175), hiddenIntKey++ is incremented unconditionally before checking !stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey) at lines 1039 and 1179. When a non-suppressed [MessagePackObject] has duplicate string keys followed by another string-keyed member (e.g., during IDE editing when the incremental generator still runs), stringMembers stores non-contiguous IntKey values (such as 0 and 2 for 2 members), risking out-of-bounds indexing if string-key formatter generation assumes contiguous 0..Count-1 indices.

All four MsgPack005 tests in SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs declare only properties, so none of the crash-fix changes in the field member loop (lines 1148, 1163-1166, and 1179-1182) are exercised by any test.
